proposition.claim:
A chord-arc Jordan curve \(\Gamma\) has a constant \(C\) such that the length \(\ell(x,y)\) of its shorter connecting subarc satisfies \(|x-y|\leq\ell(x,y)\leq C|x-y|\). Its unit tangent \(\tau\) exists almost everywhere. The central Euclidean comparison concerns \[\operatorname{M\ddot ob}(\Gamma)
 =\int_\Gamma\!\int_\Gamma\left(\frac1{|z-w|^2}-\frac1{\ell(z,w)^2}\right)|dz|\,|dw|
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \int_\Gamma\!\int_\Gamma\frac{|\tau(x)-\tau(y)|^2}{|x-y|^2}|dx|\,|dy|.\] These are nonnegative integrals; Tonelli is available even before finiteness is known. The admissible integration domain after interchanging variables still matters.

The geometric conditions include a scale-normalized \(\beta\) number for \(3Q\cap\Gamma\), a reflection-distortion number \(\rho(Q)\) measuring Euclidean departure from isometry, and a fat-ball quantity \(\varepsilon_\Gamma(Q)\). In hyperbolic upper-half-space the operative metric for the curvature/area calculations is \(ds_\rho^2=(|dx|^2+dt^2)/t^2\), of curvature \(-1\). The thickness \(\delta\) of the hyperbolic convex hull vanishes for a round circle. A totally geodesic hemisphere then has both principal curvatures zero. These elementary special cases obey, rather than evade, the hypotheses used in Problems 2 and 3.

For a minimal surface \(S\subset\mathbb H^3\), its principal curvatures are \(\pm\kappa\), and \(K=-1-\kappa^2\). For a regular height truncation \(S_t\), \[A_\rho(S_t)-L_\rho(\partial S_t)
 =-2\pi\chi(S_t)-\int_{S_t}\kappa^2\,dA_\rho
   +\int_{\partial S_t}(\kappa_g-1)\,dL_\rho.\] The final boundary integral must tend to zero to obtain the stated formula for renormalized area. Finiteness of an area integral by itself is not a pointwise or trace estimate.

Upper Fubini product-domain kernel is comparable to |x-y|^-2.

Retain a+b+d<=length/2; chord-arc gives kernel upper <=2C^4/(6d^2), lower from a,b in [0,d]; large separated pairs bounded.

Requires Euclidean scale term, foliation justification and an L2 local-supremum estimate; no general replacement proved.
